narrative:
The model estimates a 36% chance that you will not pass your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your preparation.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is that you have already failed three classes in the past. Among students who passed, the average number of prior failures is zero, so this history strongly pushes the model toward expecting you to fail again. The second most important factor is that you are receiving extra educational support at school. This actually works in your favor and pulls the prediction back toward passing, because the model has learned that students who get this help tend to improve their chances. The third notable influence is that your father is your guardian. This also nudges the outcome slightly toward passing compared with students whose mothers or other relatives act as guardian.

Taken together, your past academic setbacks outweigh the helpful signals from the support you receive and your family setup, leading the model to conclude you are at real risk.

To improve, focus first on breaking the pattern of repeated failures. Speak with your teachers about targeted help in the subjects that have been hardest, make full use of the extra educational support already available to you, and consider adding consistent daily study time. Small, steady changes now can still shift your final outcome. (218 words)
